## ServiceNow, Inc. (CIK 1373715) — Operating Expense Profile, FY2022–FY2024

**Period used:** fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2024, 2023 and 2022, from the FY2024 Form 10-K (accession 0001373715-25-000010, filed 2025). All figures are consolidated, undimensioned, USD; the same values are corroborated by the prior-year 10-Ks (0001373715-24-000030, 0001373715-23-000035), so no duplicate-summing issue arises.

### Disclosed values (USD millions)

| Metric | FY2022 | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY24 vs FY23 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue (RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax) | 7,245 | 8,971 | 10,984 | +22.4% |
| **Total operating expenses** (OperatingExpenses) | 5,317 | 6,288 | 7,333 | +16.6% |
| Sales & marketing | 2,814 | 3,301 | 3,854 | +16.8% |
| Research & development | 1,768 | 2,124 | 2,543 | +19.7% |
| General & administrative | 735 | 863 | 936 | +8.5% |
| Cost of revenue | 1,573 | 1,921 | 2,287 | +19.1% |
| Operating income | 355 | 762 | 1,364 | +79% |

### Derived ratios (calculations, not disclosed fields)
- **Opex / revenue:** 73.4% (FY22) → 70.1% (FY23) → **66.8% (FY24)** — about 6.6 points of deleveraging reversed into leverage over two years.
- **S&M / revenue:** 38.8% (FY22) → 36.8% (FY23) → **35.1% (FY24)** (report states 37% → 35%).
- **R&D / revenue:** 24.4% → 23.7% → **23.2%** (report states 24% → 23%).
- **G&A / revenue:** ~10.1% → ~9.6% → **8.5%** (report states 10% → 9%).
- **Operating margin:** 4.9% → 8.5% → **12.4%**.

### What changed
1. **Expenses grew, but slower than revenue.** Total opex rose $1,045M (+16.6%) in FY2024 versus revenue growth of 22.4%, so every major function declined as a share of revenue. The mix stayed stable — S&M remained the largest block (~53% of total opex), R&D ~35%, G&A ~13% — so the change is one of *scale efficiency*, not reallocation between functions.
2. **G&A was the most restrained line** (+8.5%, only $73M), and the 10-K attributes it to higher headcount/personnel costs (+$37M) and other corporate/outside services (+$67M), **partly offset by a $36M decrease in stock-based compensation** as performance-award service periods were met.
3. **R&D and S&M drove the dollar increase**, both headcount-led: R&D +$419M (personnel +$350M, outside services +$48M, data-center software/maintenance +$27M, partly offset by −$12M program spend); S&M +$553M (personnel +$330M, deferred-commission amortization +$90M, program/branding/events +$95M).
4. **Stock-based compensation** rose to $1,746M from $1,604M (+9%) but fell to 16% of revenue from 18%, with S&M SBC +$60M and R&D SBC +$76M offset by G&A SBC −$36M.

### Limitations
- FY2022 ratios for S&M/G&A are derived from the same disclosed dollar figures; the FY2024 10-K's narrative percentage-of-revenue disclosures cover only 2024 vs 2023.
- Management's statements about FY2025 (opex up in absolute dollars but flat-to-slightly-down as a % of revenue) are **forward-looking expectations, not results**, and are excluded from the trend above.
- The database snapshot also contains 2025 quarterly data (e.g., Q1 2025 opex $1,986M; Q2 2025 $2,133M), but these are partial-year flows and are not comparable to the annual figures, so they are not used here.
